ratings_why.fun: A good growth shape: cheap early losses while hero damage is 0, then the pile and the Fruit count both scale, and you choose each turn whether to bury, add Fruit or add deaths.
ratings_why.distinct: The shared overnight pile and Bootlace's run being cut by your own burials feel fresh, but the death-feeds-stats core is close to Battlegrounds Undead and Hearthstone corpses.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken as written; the hot spots are high rolls for the owner to dial, and another pass would mostly reshuffle the same three levers.

points.text: Turns 4 to 7 look thin: hero damage starts, but the only Fruit before Tier 3 is the Apprentice. A Tier 2 Fruit unit or a cheaper Sealbearer would carry the climb into the midgame.

White-Rot Renderer is where Fruit growth flows back into the pile: bury a pumped unit and every Fruit unit drinks a quarter of it. Keep it hot, but give the owner a lever, such as 'Once a turn' across all your Renderers.
Rootbinder does nothing on a mono-Guild board. 'Units beside this have Fruit; units of other tribes have it twice' keeps the splash pull and stops it being a dead buy.
Spores make Hired Mute free gold every turn from mid-game on. Scaling it (1 gold per 4 deaths, up to 3) would make it a real choice between economy and a board slot.
Show 'tomorrow's Fruit' (a quarter of the pile) next to the Compost tracker in the shop, so the bury-or-keep choice is something you can read.

standouts.why: Grandmother Bootlace is a real capstone, and her touching run clashes with your own burials, so placement becomes the skill test.
Clerk Inkcap is a clean Tier 4 multiplier with a cost built in: he doubles each fight death and shrinks while he does it.
Warden Amanita names the comp: she trades board for death triggers before a blow is struck.

weakest.why: Rootbinder is dead text unless you are splashing another tribe.
Moss-Bier Bearer is a generic buff from a neighbour's death, with no hook into Compost or Fruit.
Stumpwick Grandsire makes 1/2 Spores at printed size, a poor Tier 5 unless you have fed it already.

flags.note: Golden Mourner keeps the whole pile, so it grows every turn and each Fruit unit drinks a quarter of it: quadratic growth, the likeliest runaway.
Renderer burying a Fruit-pumped unit at full stats sends Fruit growth back into the pile; with golden Renderer, Bootlace and Mourner it compounds turn on turn.
Bootlace plus two Sealbearers puts four Fruits on one carry, a big high roll worth the owner's eye.
Golden Old Fingers' copies keep all their stats and re-fire Puffling and Grandsire death text, which is very large even at six times a fight.
Three deaths a turn is easy with Spores, so Hired Mute is near-free gold.
